formatting.fileFormat: Word document. "For submission and review, please submit the manuscript as a Word document. Do not submit your manuscript in PDF format." Figures as separate files (1 file per figure); tables at the end of the manuscript file, not as images or separate files. Recommended file sizes: individual files no more than 500 kB and not exceeding 1 MB; total for all files not exceeding 5 MB (not including video).
formatting.font: 10-, 11-, or 12-point font size ("Use 10-, 11-, or 12-point font size, double-space text, and leave right margins unjustified (ragged).")
formatting.margins: Right margins unjustified (ragged); no numeric margin widths are stated
formatting.pageNumbers: "Start each of these sections on a new page, numbered consecutively, beginning with the title page."
formatting.referenceStyle: AMA Manual of Style (11th edition). "Number references in the order they appear in the text; do not alphabetize." "In text, tables, and legends, identify references with superscript arabic numerals." "List all authors and/or editors up to 6; if more than 6, list the first 3 followed by 'et al.'" Journal references include the issue number in parentheses after the volume number; abbreviate journal names per PubMed. "AI, LLM, and chatbots should not be used to generate or format references." Personal communications are not included in the reference list.
formatting.coverLetter: Recommended, not required: "A cover letter is recommended with complete contact information for the corresponding author" (tag: Include: JNO). The other JAMA Network journals' "Include a cover letter" wording is tagged Exclude: JNO.
formatting.supplement: Section is titled "Supplement" (tag: Include: JNO and JHF), not "Online-Only Supplement". "Supplemental material should be submitted in a single Word document with pages numbered consecutively." Items are cited in the main text and "numbered in order of citation in the text (eg, eTable 1, eTable 2, eFigure 1, eFigure 2, eMethods)"; the first page lists the number and title of each element. "Supplemental text should be set in Times New Roman font, 10 point in size, and single-spaced" (main heading 12 pt bold, subheadings 10 pt bold). "The text and data in supplemental tables should be Arial font, 10 point in size, and single-spaced" (titles Arial 12 pt bold; footnotes 8 pt). Supplemental figure titles Arial 12 pt bold, legends 8 pt; photographs .jpg or .tif at 300 dpi, 3-5 inches wide. Supplement references go in a separate reference section. "This material will not be edited or formatted; thus, authors are responsible for the accuracy and presentation". Trial protocols with complete statistical analysis plans "should be cited in the Methods section and submitted as supplemental content" and are published as a Supplement. The Data Sharing Statement is "published in a Data Sharing Statement in an online supplement linked to the published article." Analysis code, if included, goes in the supplemental content. "the journal is not a data repository"; large datasets go to public repositories.
formatting.titlePage: First page of the manuscript file. "It should include a manuscript title; the full names, highest academic degrees, and affiliations of all authors" (if an author's affiliation changed since the work was done, list the new affiliation too); "name and complete contact information for corresponding author"; "manuscript word count (not including title, abstract, acknowledgment, references, tables, and figure legends)".

abstracts.other: "Include a structured abstract." "Do not use abbreviations in the title or abstract and limit their use in the text." No information may appear in the abstract that is not in the text. Research Letters: "They should not include an abstract or key points". "Abstracts are not required for Invited Commentaries." (tag: Include: JNO and JHF). An "Alternate Abstract for Special Communication (350 words)" with headings Importance / Observations / Conclusions and Relevance exists on the page but is tagged Include: JHF. "Abstracts for Trial Protocols" is tagged Include: None / Exclude: All.

keyPoints.rules: "In the manuscript, include a separate section called 'Key Points' before the Abstract." (tag: Include: Specialty Journals, JNO, JHF). "Limit this section to 75-100 words or less." "(required only for research and review manuscripts)". Question: "Focused question based on the study hypothesis or goal/purpose. Limit to 1 sentence." Findings: "Results of the study/review. Include the design (eg, clinical trial, cohort study, case-control study, meta-analysis)", primary outcomes with basic numbers and whether results are significant, without test statistics; "Can include 1 to 2 sentences." Meaning: "Key conclusion and implication based on the primary finding(s). Limit to 1 sentence." Original Investigation: "A list of 3 Key Points is required". Research Letters: no Key Points. NOTE: the 75-100 word sentence sits in shared text after a tag whose comment says it covers only the preceding 'In the manuscript...' line; one fetch read it as JAMA-only, so treat the exact limit with mild caution.

journalNotes: The instructions page is a template shared across JAMA Network journals with visible 'Include:/Exclude:' tags (JNO = JAMA Network Open). Several blocks carry conflicting tags (Systematic Review, Meta-analysis, Special Communication); conflicts are flagged in the relevant article-type notes.
Cover letter is recommended, not required ("A cover letter is recommended with complete contact information for the corresponding author", tag Include: JNO).

Supplement: the section is titled "Supplement" (not "Online-Only Supplement"); single Word document, supplemental text in Times New Roman 10 pt single-spaced, supplemental tables in Arial 10 pt; items named eTable/eFigure/eMethods in citation order. Trial protocols are published as a Supplement; the Data Sharing Statement is published in an online supplement linked to the article.

Article types tagged as NOT for JNO: Brief Report, Narrative Review, Opinion/Viewpoint, Perspective, Letters to the Editor / Letter in Reply / Correspondence, Clinical Challenge and other challenge types, Images, Humanities, Teachable Moment, Inside Story, Observation.
"If accepted for publication, all articles are published online only." (tag: Include: JNO and JHF).

Open access: all accepted articles are open access on publication following payment of article processing charges; "Payment of $4000 and grant of a Publication License to the journal." (CC-BY-NC-ND or CC-BY). "Waivers and discounts on open access article processing charges are available for eligible authors" from Hinari Core Offer countries.
"The journal uses a single-anonymized peer review process"; "Submitted manuscripts may be reviewed with software to detect plagiarism and inappropriate duplication." (tag includes JNO).
Postpublication Online Commenting (tag: Include: JNO and JHF): comments "should not exceed 600 words, including references."

"For all reports of research, authors are required to provide a Data Sharing Statement"; "Authors of research articles should follow the EQUATOR Reporting Guidelines." (tag: Include: SJs, JNO, and JHF).

The referral/transfer text ("The JAMA Network Advantage", JAMA-EXPRESS) is tagged Include: JAMA / Exclude: Specialty Journals, JNO, JHF; the JNO page does not describe manuscripts being referred into JNO.

Titles: "Please limit the length of titles to 100 characters (including spaces) for reports of research and other major articles" and "60 characters (including spaces) for shorter article types such as opinion articles" and for subtitles; avoid declarative titles, titles stating result direction, and questions.

Figures: "Do not submit figures with more than 4 panels unless otherwise justified."; "In general each figure should be no larger than 1 MB."; minimum resolution ≥350 ppi (photographs/illustrations) and ≥600 ppi (line drawings); no pie charts, 3-D graphs, or stacked bar charts. Tables single-spaced in 10- or 12-point font with titles preferably no longer than 10 to 15 words.

AI: content created by AI/LLMs is discouraged unless part of the formal research design; any AI use must be reported in the Acknowledgment section; AI may not generate or format references; AI may not draft Opinion manuscripts, Letters, or Online Comments; AI-created or -manipulated clinical images are not permitted.
Conflicts of interest and funding statements are required in the Acknowledgment section for all journals; authors without conflicts must state so.
A 'Clinical Practice Guidelines' tag (Include: JNO) sits beside the Consensus Statement section, but no separate article type or limits for guidelines appear on the page.
unread: All text was fetched in three chunks (offsets 0 and 100000; the page is 198,271 characters so offset 200000 returned nothing). However, the fetch tool summarizes the page with a small model and caps quotations at ~125 characters, so the page could not be read verbatim; values were cross-checked across multiple targeted fetches, and residual tag ambiguities are noted per article type.
